A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

morphological imaging (MR imaging and contrast-enhanced CT) should be performed to assess the presence and number of lesions, their size, location and extent, and the presence and extent of vascular and biliary infiltration.
morphological imaging (US, CT, MR, and PET/CT) is very effective in detecting NELMs and assessing their resectability, whereas the role of scintigraphy is limited.

MR imaging is the best morphological imaging approach for detecting NELMs and assessing their resectability, and that somatostatin PET is the most accurate molecular imaging modality for assessing the resectable of NELMs.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, when available, PET/CT is the imaging modality of choice for assessing the resectable of NELM, and that gadoxetic acid and diffusion-weighted MR imaging sequences should be routinely included in the MR imaging protocol for detecting and characterizing NELM.

the combined use of multiphase, gadoxetic-acid-enhanced MR imaging and somatostain receptor PET/CT is the most promising strategy for detecting NELMs, assessing their vascular and biliary infiltration, and the presence and extent of extrahepate disease.

, for the evaluation of NELM, the best imaging strategy should be tailored to the clinical context and the type of patient (i.e., symptomatic versus asymptomatic; well-differentiated versus poorly-differentiated).
